classification.difficultyReason: Fit and read a line, then compare 16 missed lessons with the observed range to explain why that prediction is unreliable.

content.prompt: A group of students sat a test at the end of term. The number of lessons each student missed during the term and their score on the test are shown on the scatterplot.

spec.description: Black scatterplot with positive axis arrows, no grid and no supplied best-fit line.
spec.mathematics: Horizontal scale 0–10, step 1; vertical scale 0–100, step 10. Points reproduce the visible source positions. Unlabelled scores near 66 and 36 are approximate pixel readings rather than numerical givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied data points are visible in the question.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Describe the strength and direction of the linear association observed in this dataset.

answer.worked: The points lie close to a downward-sloping straight line: students who missed more lessons generally had lower test scores. The linear association is strong and negative.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Calculate the range of the test scores for the students who missed no lessons.

answer.worked:
For students who missed no lessons, the highest score is $100$ and the lowest is $80$.
$$\text{Range}=100-80=20\text{ marks}.$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Draw a line of best fit on the scatterplot.

answer.short: An acceptable example is shown; other reasonable by-eye lines are possible.
answer.worked: Draw a downward-sloping straight line through the centre of the points, with roughly balanced points above and below it. One acceptable example passes near $(0,88)$ and $(9,7)$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Meg did not sit the test. She missed five lessons. Use the line of best fit drawn to estimate Meg’s score on this test.

answer.short: About $43$ marks; estimates between $41$ and $46$ depend on the line drawn.
answer.worked: From $5$ missed lessons on the horizontal axis, move vertically to the best-fit line, then horizontally to the score axis. The example line gives about $43$ marks. A reasonable line may give an estimate between $41$ and $46$.

children.label: e
children.prompt: John also did not sit the test and he missed 16 lessons. Is it appropriate to use the line of best fit to estimate his score on the test? Briefly explain your answer.

answer.short: No. $16$ missed lessons is outside the observed range, so the estimate would be unreliable extrapolation.
answer.worked: No. The data cover $0$ to $9$ missed lessons. Predicting at $16$ missed lessons would extrapolate well beyond these data, where the observed relationship may not continue.

spec.description: One acceptable by-eye best-fit line and dashed reading guides for Meg.
spec.mathematics: Example line y=88−9x, restricted to the displayed data range; at x=5 it gives y=43. This is an acceptable graphical example, not a required regression equation.
